title: Find and check a biology source
objective: Build a focused search and choose a source you can check.

slides.title: Turn a question into search words
body: For “Which birds live in city parks?”, choose birds, city and parks.
Try birds AND parks. Add urban to focus the search. Try a different word if you find too little.

slides.title: Look past the title
body: Imagine a source called “Birds after rain.” Who wrote it? Where did the counts come from?
A named author is a starting point. Check the method, date, references and fit with your question.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: You want to find papers about frogs in city ponds. Source A lists an author, a method, a date and references. Source B is an unsigned post with no sources.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Write a search with two ideas joined by AND.
Add a second word for “city” using OR.
One idea is the animal. One is the place.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: You want to find papers about bees in city gardens. Source A lists an author, a method, a date and references. Source B is an unsigned post with no sources.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Write a search with two ideas joined by AND.
Add a second word for “city” using OR.
Which source would you read first? Give two reasons.

slides.title: Keep a search note
body: Record your search words, one source you would choose, and one feature you would check before citing it.
